title: Ep 1 — Instagram Privacy Tech Turned Off
description: Instagram has removed end-to-end encryption from DMs — a major privacy U-turn by Meta. What does this mean for your messages?

title: Ep 2 — Is Being Bilingual Good for Your Brain?
description: Science shows bilingual people develop dementia 4 years later and recover better from strokes. But is it ever too late to learn?

title: Ep 3 — Why Can't We Stop Eating Certain Foods?
description: The shocking truth about ultra-processed foods — engineered to bypass your brain's satiety signals and keep you eating more.

title: Ep 4 — AI2027: Is This How AI Might Destroy Humanity?
description: A controversial research paper predicts AI will go rogue in 2027 and wipe out humanity by 2035. BBC World Service investigates.

title: Ep 5 — Life Against the Odds in Australia's Underground Town
description: In Coober Pedy, 60% of residents live underground to escape scorching heat — and the town is now a leader in renewable energy.

title: Ep 6 — Talking About Lunch
description: A natural everyday conversation about what people eat for lunch — great for practising real-life English and food vocabulary.

title: Ep 7 — Day in the Life with a Newborn at −64°C
description: A documentary following a mother through a full day in Yakutsk — the coldest inhabited city on Earth — caring for a newborn in extreme winter.

title: Ep 8 — Can Diet Improve Memory?
description: BBC News Review looks at research showing that flavanols in dark chocolate, berries and leafy greens may help keep memory sharp as we age.

title: Ep 9 — Naps: Good for Your Brain?
description: BBC News Review explores whether regular power naps can preserve brain size, keep your mind sharp and reduce the risk of Alzheimer's disease.

title: Ep 10 — First Arab Woman in Space
description: BBC News Review covers Rayyanah Barnawi's historic mission to the ISS — and teaches three key vocabulary phrases from the headlines.

title: Ep 11 — Is It Still Worth Going to University?
description: With £50,000 of debt and a changing job market, BBC asks whether a university degree is still a sound investment in 2026.
